title_en: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
title: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek, Shiran Liu, Mickael Rouvier, Jane Wottawa, Richard Dufour
content: Evaluates LLMs for ASR evaluation: 92-94% human agreement vs 63% WER on HATS dataset.
content_en: This paper evaluates decoder-based Large Language Models (LLMs) for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) evaluation through three approaches: hypothesis selection, semantic distance using generative embeddings, and qualitative error classification. On the HATS dataset, the best LLMs achieve 92-94% agreement with human annotators for hypothesis selection, compared to 63% for WER, outperforming semantic metrics. Embeddings from decoder-based LLMs show performance comparable to encoder models.

entities.domains: natural language processing, speech recognition, large language models

title_en: MathDuels: Evaluating LLMs as Problem Posers and Solvers
title: MathDuels: Evaluating LLMs as Problem Posers and Solvers
authors: Zhiqiu Xu, Shibo Jin, Shreya Arya, Mayur Naik
content: Self-play benchmark where LLMs both author and solve math problems across 19 frontier models.
content_en: MathDuels introduces a self-play benchmark where models occupy dual roles: authoring math problems under adversarial prompting and solving problems authored by others. Uses a three-stage generation pipeline and a Rasch model to estimate solver abilities and problem difficulties. Experiments across 19 frontier models reveal that authoring and solving capabilities are partially decoupled. The benchmark's difficulty co-evolves with participant strength rather than saturating at a fixed ceiling.

entities.domains: natural language processing, large language models, mathematical reasoning

title_en: GiVA: Gradient-Informed Bases for Vector-Based Adaptation
title: GiVA: Gradient-Informed Bases for Vector-Based Adaptation
authors: Neeraj Gangwar, Rishabh Deshmukh, Michael Shavlovsky, Hancao Li, Vivek Mittal, Lexing Ying, Nickvash Kani
content: Gradient-based initialization for vector adaptation, 8x rank reduction vs LoRA. AISTATS 2026.
content_en: GiVA introduces a gradient-based initialization strategy for vector-based adaptation of large language models. It achieves training times comparable to LoRA while maintaining extreme parameter efficiency. Evaluated across natural language understanding, natural language generation, and image classification benchmarks. Consistently outperforms or achieves competitive performance with existing vector-based methods and LoRA while reducing rank requirements by a factor of eight. Accepted to AISTATS 2026.

entities.domains: natural language processing, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, deep learning

title_en: Mapping the Political Discourse in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies: A Multi-Faceted Computational Approach
title: Mapping the Political Discourse in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies
authors: Flávio Soriano, Victoria F. Mello, Pedro B. Rigueira, Gisele L. Pappa, Wagner Meira Jr., Ana Paula Couto da Silva, Jussara M. Almeida
content: Computational analysis of 450K+ Brazilian parliamentary speeches 2003-2025. ICWSM 2026.
content_en: A scalable computational framework combining diachronic stylometric analysis, contextual topic modeling, and semantic clustering applied to over 450,000 speeches from the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies (2003-2025). Results show a long-term stylistic shift toward shorter speeches, a legislative agenda that reorients in response to national crises, and discursive alignments where regional and gender identities often prove more salient than party affiliation. Accepted at ICWSM 2026.

entities.domains: natural language processing, computational social science, political discourse

title_en: EVENT5Ws: A Large Dataset for Open-Domain Event Extraction from Documents
title: EVENT5Ws: A Large Dataset for Open-Domain Event Extraction from Documents
authors: Praval Sharma, Ashok Samal, Leen-Kiat Soh, Deepti Joshi
content: Large manually annotated open-domain event extraction dataset with LLM benchmarks.
content_en: EVENT5Ws is a large manually annotated and statistically verified open-domain event extraction dataset addressing limitations of existing datasets including limited event type coverage. The paper designs a systematic annotation pipeline and evaluates state-of-the-art pre-trained LLMs, establishing benchmarks. Models trained on EVENT5Ws generalize effectively to datasets from different geographical contexts.

entities.domains: natural language processing, information extraction, event extraction

title_en: TingIS: Real-time Risk Event Discovery from Noisy Customer Incidents at Enterprise Scale
title: TingIS: Real-time Risk Event Discovery from Noisy Customer Incidents at Enterprise Scale
authors: Jun Wang, Ziyin Zhang, Rui Wang, Hang Yu, Peng Di, Rui Wang
content: Enterprise incident discovery system with LLMs, 3.5min P90 latency, 95% discovery rate. ACL 2026.
content_en: TingIS is an end-to-end system for enterprise-grade incident discovery using a multi-stage event linking engine combining efficient indexing with LLMs. Includes cascaded routing for business attribution and multi-dimensional noise reduction. Deployed in production handling over 2,000 messages per minute, achieving P90 alert latency of 3.5 minutes and 95% discovery rate for high-priority incidents. Accepted to ACL 2026 Industry Track.

entities.domains: natural language processing, information extraction, industrial NLP

title_en: A Multimodal Text- and Graph-Based Approach for Open-Domain Event Extraction from Documents
title: MODEE: Multimodal Open-Domain Event Extraction
content: Graph + LLM multimodal approach for open-domain event extraction, outperforms SOTA methods.
content_en: MODEE proposes a multimodal approach for open-domain event extraction combining graph-based learning with text-based LLM representations to model document-level reasoning. Addresses limitations of closed-domain algorithms and existing open-domain methods that overlook LLMs. Empirical evaluations on large datasets show MODEE outperforms state-of-the-art open-domain methods and generalizes to closed-domain event extraction.

entities.domains: natural language processing, information extraction, graph neural networks

title_en: Revisiting Non-Verbatim Memorization in Large Language Models: The Role of Entity Surface Forms
title: Revisiting Non-Verbatim Memorization in LLMs: Entity Surface Forms
authors: Yuto Nishida, Naoki Shikoda, Yosuke Kishinami, Ryo Fujii, Makoto Morishita, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Taro Watanabe
content: RedirectQA dataset studies how entity surface forms affect LLM factual memorization. ACL 2026.
content_en: Introduces RedirectQA, an entity-based QA dataset using Wikipedia redirect information to associate Wikidata factual triples with categorized surface forms including alternative names, abbreviations, spelling variants, and erroneous forms. Across 13 LLMs, prediction outcomes often change when only the entity surface form changes. Models are more robust to minor orthographic variations than to larger lexical variations. Accepted to ACL 2026 Main.

entities.domains: natural language processing, large language models, knowledge representation

title_en: Machine Behavior in Relational Moral Dilemmas: Moral Rightness, Predicted Human Behavior, and Model Decisions
title: Machine Behavior in Relational Moral Dilemmas
authors: Jiseon Kim, Jea Kwon, Luiz Felipe Vecchietti, Wenchao Dong, Jaehong Kim, Meeyoung Cha
content: LLM moral decision-making study: models prioritize fairness over social sensitivity. ACL Findings 2026.
content_en: Characterizes machine behavior using the Whistleblower's Dilemma varying crime severity and relational closeness across three perspectives: moral rightness, predicted human behavior, and autonomous model decision-making. Analysis of reasoning processes reveals cross-perspective divergence: moral rightness remains consistently fairness-oriented while predicted human behavior shifts toward loyalty as relational closeness increases. Model decisions align with moral rightness rather than their own behavioral predictions. Accepted to ACL Findings 2026.

entities.domains: natural language processing, large language models, AI ethics

title_en: SemEval-2026 Task 4: Narrative Story Similarity and Narrative Representation Learning
title: SemEval-2026 Task 4: Narrative Story Similarity and Narrative Representation Learning
authors: Hans Ole Hatzel, Ekaterina Artemova, Haimo Paul Stiemer, Evelyn Gius, Chris Biemann
content: SemEval-2026 shared task on narrative similarity: 71 submissions from 46 teams, LLM ensembles lead.
content_en: Presents NSNRL, a shared task on narrative similarity and representation learning operationalized as binary classification: determining which of two stories is more similar to an anchor story. Collected annotations for over 1,000 story summary triples. Received 71 final submissions from 46 teams across two tracks. LLM ensembles dominate the classification track while systems with pre/post-processing on pretrained embedding models perform competitively in the embedding track.

entities.domains: natural language processing, semantic similarity, narrative understanding
